description:
What this shows: Per-job-type throughput, queue wait times, and execution times for the node's internal worker job queue.
Use it to: Find job types that are backing up or running slowly and causing internal processing delays.

panels.title: Current Job Latency (p99 Gauge) [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*At-a-glance p99 of how long jobs wait in the queue and how long they run once started.*

###### How it's computed:
*99th percentile derived from the job wait-time and run-time histograms over the last 5 minutes.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; green under 100ms, yellow to 1s, red beyond 1s.*

###### Healthy range:
*Wait and exec p99 under 100ms.*

###### Watch for:
*p99 wait climbing into the red, meaning worker threads are saturated and jobs are backing up.*

###### Keywords:
- **Job queue / job type** *(per node)* — xrpld's worker-thread pool; every unit of background work is enqueued under a named job type.
- **Deferred job** *(per node)* — a job held back because its type is already at its concurrency limit; the leading indicator of queue backpressure.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in xrpld code as a native metric (beast::insight); the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`recordJobStarted / recordJobFinished`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#job-queue-job-type)

targets.expr: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_node_role, xrpl_work_item) (rate(job_queued_us_bucket{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", job_type=~"$job_type", handler=~"$handler"}[5m]))), "series", "p99 Wait", "", "")

panels.title: Job Throughput Rate (Per Second)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of jobs queued, started, and finished across all job types.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of each cumulative job counter over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Queued, started, and finished tracking together means the queue keeps up.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; the three rates should stay roughly equal.*

###### Watch for:
*Queued rate persistently above finished rate, which indicates a growing backlog.*

###### Keywords:
- **Job queue / job type** *(per node)* — xrpld's worker-thread pool; every unit of background work is enqueued under a named job type.
- **Deferred job** *(per node)* — a job held back because its type is already at its concurrency limit; the leading indicator of queue backpressure.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in xrpld code as a native metric (beast::insight); the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`recordJobQueued / recordJobStarted / recordJobFinished`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#job-queue-job-type)

panels.title: Job Queue Wait Time
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How long jobs sit in the queue before a worker picks them up, split by job type (p75 typical, p99 tail).*

###### How it's computed:
*Percentiles derived from the job wait-time histogram over a 5-minute window, kept per job type. Limited to the ten types with the highest wait so the legend stays readable.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better. The legend names the job type, so a single slow queue is identifiable rather than hidden in an all-types average. A widening p75-to-p99 gap on one type signals occasional stalls there.*

###### Healthy range:
*Sub-millisecond to low-millisecond waits on an unloaded node.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising p99 wait on a capped type -- ledgerRequest, ledgerData and makeFetchPack have small concurrency limits, so they queue first. Cross-check the deferred gauge for that type.*

###### Keywords:
- **Job queue** *(per node)* — the worker pool that runs xrpld's background work; each unit of work is a job with a type.
- **Dequeue wait** *(per node)* — time a job sits enqueued before a worker starts it, as distinct from how long it then runs.
- **Concurrency limit** *(per node)* — the maximum number of jobs of one type allowed to run at once; work beyond it is deferred, not rejected.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node and job type — each series is one server's own value for one job type.*
*Recorded in code as an OTel SDK histogram, then aggregated to percentiles by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`recordJobStarted`

###### References:
[Job queue](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#job-queue-job-type) · [Concurrency limit](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#concurrency-limit)

panels.title: Job Execution Time
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How long jobs run once started, split by job type (p75 typical, p99 tail).*

###### How it's computed:
*Percentiles derived from the job run-time histogram over a 5-minute window, kept per job type. Limited to the ten slowest types so the legend stays readable.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better. The legend names the job type, so an expensive job type is identifiable rather than averaged away. Stable p75 with a controlled p99 is healthy.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent, but stable over time.*

###### Watch for:
*Growing execution times, which point to CPU pressure or expensive individual jobs.*

###### Keywords:
- **Job queue** *(per node)* — the worker pool that runs xrpld's background work; each unit of work is a job with a type.
- **Execution time** *(per node)* — time a job spends running after a worker picks it up, excluding its queue wait.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node and job type — each series is one server's own value for one job type.*
*Recorded in code as an OTel SDK histogram, then aggregated to percentiles by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`recordJobFinished`

###### References:
[Job queue](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#job-queue-job-type)

panels.title: Transaction Overflow Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate at which transaction jobs are shed when the queue's transaction limit is exceeded.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the overflow counter over the dashboard's rate interval, scaled to per minute. The counter is observed from the overlay's cumulative overflow tally.*

###### Reading it:
*Near zero is healthy; a rising rate means the job queue is shedding transaction work under load.*

###### Healthy range:
*0 overflows per minute.*

###### Watch for:
*Any sustained non-zero rate — the node is dropping transaction jobs because the queue is saturated.*

###### Keywords:
- **Job queue / job type** *(per node)* — xrpld's worker-thread pool; every unit of background work is enqueued under a named job type.
- **Transaction queue (TxQ)** *(per node)* — holds transactions that cannot enter the open ledger yet, ordered by fee level.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in xrpld code as a native metric (beast::insight); the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerParityCounters (observed from Overlay::getJqTransOverflow)`

[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#job-queue-job-type)
